contexts.text: Abram... dwelt in the oak-groves of Mamre, which are in Hebron () = that the Lord arrived at a perception still more interior... This perception is called the oak-groves of Mamre which are in Hebron. Mamre is mentioned in other places also. Illustrated.
He was dwelling in the oak-groves of Mamre the Amorite () = a state of perception from the rational man; as is evident from the signification of... the oak-groves of Mamre the Amorite. References.

By Mamre, Eshcol, and Aner () are represented... the Angels who were with the Lord when He fought in His first childhood, who were adequate to the goods and truths then with the Lord. They are named from these goods and truths. Explained.

By Mamre, Eshcol, and Aner was signified the state of the rational man as to the Lord's External, and the quality of its goods and truths; and thus by them are signified the Angels who were with the Lord when He fought. AC 1754, Explained.
The state at that time of the Lord's perception in the Human is signified by the oak-groves of Mamre (). AC 2144. AC 2145, Explained.
Machpelah which is before Mamre () = regeneration. (Machpelah = regeneration; and Mamre, the quality and quantity thereof. AC 2970.)

Mamre, being Hebron, as is said in (), and in Hebron () = nothing else than the quality and the quantity; here, of regeneration, when it is adjoined to Machpelah; and of the Church, when it is adjoined to Hebron; and also that of perception, when it is adjoined to oak-groves. Thus Mamre is only the determination of the state of a thing; for it was the place where Abraham dwelt; and where Isaac dwelt, and to which Jacob came. Illustrated.
Upon the faces of Mamre () = as to good...
Mamre Kirjath-arba () = the state thereof; (for) Mamre = the quality and quantity of that to which it is adjoined. AC 6456. AC 6551.
